title: Core Loop Completion Sprint
specification:
# Core Loop Completion Sprint

This PRD is intentionally multi-lane. PM should decompose it into three implementation lanes:
- `aquarium-agent`
- `adventure-agent`
- `action-agent`

## Product Goal

Convert the strongest existing gameplay scaffolding in each project into complete player-facing loops instead of leaving the best hooks as menus, placeholders, contracts, or half-finished services.

Player outcomes:
- Aquarium should gain real alternate session variants and one more meaningful emergency tool.
- Adventure should gain real journal / roster / town-service surfaces that make progression and companion management legible.
- Fluxborne should gain stronger combat feel, clearer build identity, and more rewarding home-base continuity.

This sprint should prefer finishing existing high-value hooks over inventing disconnected new systems.

## Sprint Shape

- 16 to 22 implementation tasks total
- 4 to 6 tasks for `aquarium-agent`
- 4 to 6 tasks for `adventure-agent`
- 6 to 10 tasks for `action-agent`
- one shared branch per implementation lane
- one PR per lane
- no PM-generated reviewer tasks

Each task should still be atomic enough for one commit.

## Scope Boundaries

Stay inside:
- `aquarium-agent` -> `src/barebones-starter/games/apps/aquarium/**`
- `adventure-agent` -> `src/barebones-starter/games/apps/adventure/**`
- `action-agent` -> `src/barebones-starter/games/apps/fluxborne/**`

PM must not generate tasks that mix project directories in the same implementation task.

## Cross-Project Engineering Intent

Prefer extending existing lane-local systems, persistence, HUD, menus, and tests before adding brand-new parallel abstractions.

Bias task planning toward:
- turning placeholder buttons, hidden modes, and message-only menus into real flows
- reusing existing state, progression, and service contracts
- preserving clean project separation

Avoid:
- docs-only filler tasks
- speculative architecture work without direct player-facing payoff
- duplicate systems where a nearby implementation can be extended

## Concrete Direction

The best improvements here are mostly about finishing loops you already scaffolded, not adding another huge subsystem.

Adventure should get real Journal, Roster, and Town Services screens. Those menu entries currently only write messages in `src/barebones-starter/games/shared/config.ts:123`, but there is already rich run-summary/objective/reputation data in `src/barebones-starter/games/apps/adventure/logic/runSummary.ts:120` and `src/barebones-starter/games/apps/adventure/logic/objectives.ts:208`. That is low-risk depth.

Aquarium should branch into actual rule variants. `Time Trial`, `Challenge`, and `Virtual Tank` are stubbed in `src/barebones-starter/games/shared/config.ts:222`, and there is already a stage/run system in `src/barebones-starter/games/apps/aquarium/logic/progression.ts:87`. Reuse the same actors with different goals instead of building a new game mode from scratch.

Aquarium also has an obvious next-button win: the potion slot is still a placeholder in `src/barebones-starter/games/apps/aquarium/actors/index.ts:427`. Turn that into a real panic tool like heal-all, pest stun, or temporary coin magnet.

Fluxborne should keep following its own roadmap: combat feel first. The design docs explicitly prioritize hit-stop, flinch, screen FX, better damage numbers, audio layering, and death variety in `docs/design/IMPLEMENTATION_ROADMAP.md:33`. That will move the project more than another content branch.

Fluxborne build identity needs to be more immediate. Skill paths are mostly contracts/definitions right now in `src/barebones-starter/games/apps/fluxborne/game/skillPath/skillPath.ts:1` and `src/barebones-starter/games/apps/fluxborne/game/skillPath/pathAbilityRegistry.ts:1`. Give each path one unmistakable early signature move or passive so the choice changes play immediately.

Fluxborne home-base ownership is another strong win. Contracts and endless continuity already exist in `src/barebones-starter/games/apps/fluxborne/components/HomeBaseHub.tsx:735`, but companion recruiting is still generic in `src/barebones-starter/games/apps/fluxborne/components/homeBase/CompanionQuartersRoom.tsx:100`, and armory favorites are still stubbed in `src/barebones-starter/games/apps/fluxborne/game/homeBase/services/armoryServices.ts:1`. Named recruits, bond perks, favorite gear/loadout compare, and stronger trophy-room callbacks would help a lot.

Priority order:
1. Fluxborne combat juice
2. Aquarium alternate modes
3. Adventure journal / roster UI

PM should preserve that priority bias when decomposing the sprint.

## Lane Deliverable Themes

### Aquarium Lane

- turn `Time Trial`, `Challenge`, and/or `Virtual Tank` into real selectable rule variants using the existing aquarium progression and run-state systems
- replace the potion placeholder with a meaningful emergency or utility action
- improve stage prompt clarity, threat telegraphing, recovery pacing, and shop readability
- make alternate modes feel distinct without abandoning the current aquarium core loop

### Adventure Lane

- replace message-only `Journal`, `Roster`, and `Town Services` actions with real surfaces, overlays, or in-game panels
- expose biome reputation, vendor/training unlocks, objectives, captures, and recent run history more clearly
- deepen the utility of captured companions and town interactions using the existing roster, training, and summary systems
- improve run-to-run continuity so the player can understand what was achieved and what to do next

### Fluxborne Lane

- prioritize combat satisfaction improvements such as hit-stop, enemy reaction, screen feedback, damage-number polish, audio layering, and kill payoff using existing combat feedback infrastructure where possible
- turn skill path contracts and build-state scaffolding into a more immediate player-facing identity
- strengthen home-base utility through armory, workshop, companion, contract, and trophy-hall improvements using existing persistence and service layers
- make progression and build state easier to read in combat and in heavy-system menus

## Planning Rules For PM

- Generate implementation tasks only.
- Do not emit reviewer tasks.
- Keep every task lane-pure and atomic.
- Prefer feature work over notes, placeholder copy, or speculative refactors.
- When a subsystem already has tests, include meaningful test coverage in the corresponding task acceptance.
- Use existing files and directories as the basis for task decomposition.
- Make the task list large enough that each lane PR becomes a real multi-commit sprint.

## Definition Of Done

- Aquarium has at least one real additional play variant and one completed utility/action loop.
- Adventure has real progression-management surfaces instead of message-only menu stubs.
- Fluxborne combat feels better and build/home-base progression is more legible and rewarding.
- The work lands as three substantial lane PRs with clear separation and without obvious duplicate systems.
